requirements.requirement: datauser limited to 100 MB of storage under /srv/data on node1
requirements.summary: A dedicated XFS filesystem was mounted at /srv/data with uquota, and datauser was given a 100M soft/hard XFS user quota. A 150M write by datauser failed exactly at 100M with 'Disk quota exceeded', both before and after a full node restart.

requirements.requirement: Limit is enforced by the filesystem itself, not application-level
requirements.summary: Enforcement uses XFS's native kernel-level user quota subsystem (usrquota mount option, xfs_quota limit), and the write was rejected by the kernel/dd itself, not by an application-layer check.
An /etc/fstab entry was added for the loop-mounted quota filesystem; unmount+mount -a reloaded it with usrquota and the 100M limit intact, and this was independently reconfirmed after a full reboot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id, quota/mount state; systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged before disconnect; connection failures during the outage confirm the node was down; boot_id changed post-restart (cross-checked by the fixed global before/after-executor boot-identity observations); post-restart quota mount, limit, and enforcement (150M write failing at 100M) were directly re-verified.

overall_summary: The executor correctly implemented a 100MB filesystem-level quota for datauser under /srv/data on node1 using a dedicated XFS loop-mounted filesystem with native usrquota enforcement, since the root filesystem could not be reconfigured with quota options live. Enforcement, persistence, and recovery after a genuine full node restart were all directly demonstrated with kernel-rejected writes at exactly 100M, and cleanup left no residue.
limitations: The quota-enabled filesystem is a separate loop-mounted image rather than a quota on the node's existing root filesystem; this is a reasonable and arguably necessary workaround given the noquota root fs, and it still satisfies the literal requirement that /srv/data be quota-limited, but it is a materially different implementation than adding quota to an existing mountpoint.
Only a single managed node (node1) exists in this topology, so no cross-node restart evidence comparison was possible or needed.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to the task: creating the quota-backed filesystem and user (cmd-1968f4644bc04d44, cmd-aa9bc09718ee4b8f), persisting via fstab (cmd-604e9aa195544373), bounded verification writes that were deleted immediately after (cmd-4388ab6e674445d0, cmd-b5e4925952de4cff, cmd-8d99d6e3510e4871, cmd-4b83600c41ed4aa9), and the reboot used for the mandated restart-evidence protocol (cmd-f6a41af58e0b4051). No abandoned residue, failed services, unnecessary mutations, or weakened security controls were observed; the after-executor lifecycle snapshot shows only expected boot-tied /tmp entries and no new failed services or listening sockets beyond the same sshd/chronyd endpoints reopened after reboot.
